probe: E2 Tier 1: does the assumed tagset exist, and do the recipes work as written?
environment: kiwipiepy 0.23.2 on Python 3.9.6, throwaway venv, removed afterwards. Nothing installed into the system Python.

tagset.verdict: VERIFIED. All 20 tags the document names exist and mean what it assumed (Sejong tagset): EF EC ETM EP JKG JKS JKO JKB JX JC NNG NNP NNB XSN MAG MAJ VV VA VX NP.
tagset.caveat: Irregular stems get subtype tags (VV-I, VV-R), so a tag == 'VV' test silently misses them. Prefix matching is required and no recipe said so.

recipes.verdict: The tagset was fine. The recipes were not. Two of them are broken as literally written, and both are fixable.

noun_ending_ratio.bug: kiwipiepy emits sentence-final punctuation as a trailing SF morpheme AFTER the EF token, so 'is the final morpheme EF' is false for every period-terminated sentence.
noun_ending_ratio.evidence: 이 기능은 값을 검증합니다. -> last three tags ['XSV','EF','SF']
noun_ending_ratio.fix: Pop trailing SF/SP/SS/SE/SO/SW before testing the final tag.
noun_ending_ratio.note: Naive, this measurement fires at 100% on all text and separates nothing. Fixed, it separates perfectly on this corpus - the strongest result in the battery.

particle_absence_ratio.bug: N + XSV (the 하다/-하 verbalizing suffix) puts a non-J* tag directly after the noun, and that is the dominant verb-formation pattern in formal Korean. Correct prose scored 0.50; correct honorific prose scored 0.80, because XSN (님) also sits between the noun and its particle.
particle_absence_ratio.evidence: correct prose flagged 입력/XSV 검증/XSV 저장/XSV 실패/XSV 표시/XSV 중단/XSV - none of them a dropped 조사. 사용자님께서 tokenises as 사용자/NNG 님/XSN 께서/JKS.
particle_absence_ratio.fix: A 체언 followed by XSV/XSA is a verb stem, not a noun awaiting a particle: drop it from the denominator. Skip XSN/XSM when looking for the following J*.
particle_absence_ratio.residual: The technical-compound case sits at 0.40, the closest of the correct cases to the defective range - the false positive E2 predicted, now measured.

other_findings: The exclusion pass must run on raw text lines BEFORE kiwipiepy's sentence splitter, not after. The splitter is paragraph-aware but knows nothing of markdown: consecutive bullets merge into one 'sentence' and a three-line table merges into another, after which individual lines cannot be attributed back. E2's phrasing implied the reverse order.
noun_run_length's 'no J* between' is ambiguous - strict consecutive NN* versus bridging over non-noun non-particle tags give very different numbers. Undecided in E2.
genitive_ui_ratio's predicted false positive is untested: no test case contained 의 at all.
A path's internal period is tagged SF at token level, but split_into_sents does not split there. A recipe that split on SF tags instead of using the splitter would break mid-path.
디렉터리 was tagged NNP rather than NNG - a tagger-accuracy risk for proper_noun_preservation in Tier 2.
